children.title: Trump DOJ Orders Review of FBI Personnel Tied to January 6 Cases
children.description_medium: Acting Deputy Attorney General Emil Bove ordered personnel actions and a review of FBI employees who had worked on January 6 cases on January 31, 2025.  This action took place before Kash Patel became FBI director, so it is attributable to Trump Justice Department leadership rather than Patel as bureau director.
children.description_long: Acting Deputy Attorney General Emil Bove ordered personnel actions and a review of FBI employees who had worked on January 6 cases on January 31, 2025. This action took place before Kash Patel became FBI director, so it is attributable to Trump Justice Department leadership rather than Patel as bureau director. Reuters reported the broad review and personnel changes. The event documents the pre-Patel review only; it does not establish a loyalty test or support the original card’s claim that Patel fired hundreds of agents. Reuters reported the January 31 review before Patel became director; the later Washington Post reports describe distinct 2025 and 2026 firing episodes under his leadership. The available evidence therefore supports a chronology of several actions, each with its own scope, rather than one continuous event beginning at Patel’s confirmation. The distinction also matters for attribution: the first action came from acting deputy attorney general Emil Bove, while the later dismissals were FBI actions. The sources identify personnel links to investigations, but do not establish that investigative assignments alone determined each employment decision or demonstrate a department-wide loyalty policy.

children.title: FBI Under Patel Fires Three Senior Officials Tied to Sensitive Investigations
children.description_medium: On August 7, 2025, the FBI dismissed at least three senior officials, including former acting director Brian Driscoll, during a broader reshuffling under FBI Director Kash Patel.  The officials had connections to January 6 or other politically sensitive investigations, according to The Washington Post.  This was a later personnel episode than the January 2025 Justice Department review and should be described on its own date.

children.title: Patel-Era FBI Fires Agents Linked to Trump Investigations
children.description_medium: On February 26, 2026, the FBI dismissed at least a dozen agents whose work was connected directly or indirectly to investigations involving Donald Trump’s classified documents or efforts to overturn the 2020 election.  The Washington Post reported the firings as a further episode under Patel, separate from the August 2025 dismissals of senior officials and the earlier personnel review ordered before Patel took office.
